atoms.name: mod
atoms.rule: a % b is the remainder a - b * (a / b), with the sign of a (-7 % 2 = -1); b = 0 gives NaN.
atoms.plain: a % b is the remainder a - b * (a / b), with the sign of a (-7 % 2 = -1); b = 0 gives NaN.

atoms.name: neg
atoms.rule: - a is the negation of a.
atoms.plain: - a is the negation of a.

atoms.name: pitch_transpose
atoms.rule: a ♯ b moves MIDI note a by b semitones; a result outside 0 through 127 gives NaN.
atoms.plain: a ♯ b moves MIDI note a by b semitones; a result outside 0 through 127 gives NaN.

atoms.name: pitch_octave_up
atoms.rule: a ⇈ raises MIDI note a by 12 semitones; a result above 127 gives NaN.
atoms.plain: a ⇈ raises MIDI note a by 12 semitones; a result above 127 gives NaN.

atoms.name: pitch_octave_down
atoms.rule: a ⇊ lowers MIDI note a by 12 semitones; a result below 0 gives NaN.
atoms.plain: a ⇊ lowers MIDI note a by 12 semitones; a result below 0 gives NaN.

atoms.name: pitch_interval
atoms.rule: a ⟷ b is the signed number of semitones from note a to note b.
atoms.plain: a ⟷ b is the signed number of semitones from note a to note b.

atoms.name: pitch_invert
atoms.rule: a ⇅ b reflects every pitch in melody a around MIDI note b and keeps durations; an out of range pitch gives NaN.
atoms.plain: a ⇅ b reflects every pitch in melody a around MIDI note b and keeps durations; an out of range pitch gives NaN.

atoms.name: pitch_retrograde
atoms.rule: a ⟲ reverses the order of melody a, keeping each note with its duration.
atoms.plain: a ⟲ reverses the order of melody a, keeping each note with its duration.

atoms.name: pitch_scale_step
atoms.rule: a ♬ is the next higher note in C major; no higher MIDI note gives NaN.
atoms.plain: a ♬ is the next higher note in C major; no higher MIDI note gives NaN.

atoms.name: pitch_major_triad
atoms.rule: a △ builds a three note major triad at MIDI note a with intervals 0, 4, 7 and one beat each; an out of range pitch gives NaN.
atoms.plain: a △ builds a three note major triad at MIDI note a with intervals 0, 4, 7 and one beat each; an out of range pitch gives NaN.

atoms.name: pitch_minor_triad
atoms.rule: a ▽ builds a three note minor triad at MIDI note a with intervals 0, 3, 7 and one beat each; an out of range pitch gives NaN.
atoms.plain: a ▽ builds a three note minor triad at MIDI note a with intervals 0, 3, 7 and one beat each; an out of range pitch gives NaN.

atoms.name: pitch_repeat
atoms.rule: a ⥁ b repeats melody a b times for b from 0 through 16; other counts give NaN.
atoms.plain: a ⥁ b repeats melody a b times for b from 0 through 16; other counts give NaN.

atoms.name: pitch_concat
atoms.rule: a ⋈ b plays melody a followed by melody b.
atoms.plain: a ⋈ b plays melody a followed by melody b.

atoms.name: pitch_melody_equal
atoms.rule: a ≎ b is true when melodies a and b have the same pitches and beat durations.
atoms.plain: a ≎ b is true when melodies a and b have the same pitches and beat durations.

atoms.name: pitch_note_equal
atoms.rule: a ≐ b is true when the two MIDI notes have the same pitch.
atoms.plain: a ≐ b is true when the two MIDI notes have the same pitch.

domain.en: A note is a MIDI number from 0 to 127; 60 is C4. A melody is a list of notes with durations in beats.
Integers give semitone steps, repeat counts and recursive counts.

settings.en: The key and scale used by the scale step ♬.
A recursive call repeats its step at most this many times; larger counts give NaN.

why.en: These atoms are one example. Atoms are chosen by the user: any function with a rule can be registered and the same three composition forms grow operators from it.

operators.name: ♢₁
operators.plain: Measure the semitones from C4 to a moved by b semitones.

operators.name: ♥₂
operators.plain: If a equals [D4:1 F4:2], reverse the notes in a, then apply ♧₂₉ to the result and 0; otherwise reverse the notes in a.

operators.name: ◇₃
operators.definition: a ◇₃ b = { a, if b == 0; (a ◇₃ (b - 1)) ♬, if b > 0 and b <= 4; (a ◇₃ (b + 1)) ♬, if b < 0 and b >= - 4 }
operators.plain: Start with a. Repeat |b| times (for b from -4 to 4; other values give NaN): move the current value up one step of C major.

operators.name: ■₄
operators.plain: Apply ♢₁ to a and b, then subtract 4 from it.

operators.name: □₅

operators.name: □₈

operators.name: ●₁₂

operators.name: ○₁₃
operators.plain: Measure the semitones from C5 to the next C major note above a.

operators.name: ○₁₄
operators.plain: Apply ♧₁₀ to a, then apply □₈ to the result and 3.

operators.name: ♧₁₅

operators.name: ●₁₆

operators.name: ◆₁₈

operators.definition: a ◆₂₁ b = { 0 - (a ■₄ b), if a ≐ 72; a ■₄ b, else }

operators.name: ♡₂₅

operators.name: ○₂₆

operators.name: ♠₂₇

operators.name: ▲₂₈

operators.name: ▲₃₀

operators.name: ♠₃₁

operators.name: ♧₃₃

operators.name: ♦₃₅

operators.name: □₄₁
